sources.title: Martin Scorsese (Q41148) -- verified live via the Wikidata API (2026-10-11): English label 'Martin Scorsese', description 'American filmmaker (born 1942)', born 17 November 1942, no date of death, citizenship United States (a second citizenship is listed, not used), Korean label present. Orientation only; not used as support for any row.

Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Martin Scorsese' biography entry -- CANONICAL SIGNIFICANCE SOURCE: introduction calls him known for harsh, often violent depictions of American culture, and 'perhaps the most significant American director of the late 20th and early 21st centuries'; the career sections give Who's That Knocking at My Door, Mean Streets (with Harvey Keitel and Robert De Niro, who did ten films with him between 1973 and 2023), Taxi Driver (Palme d'Or at Cannes), New York, New York and The Last Waltz, and the page's questions section notes his efforts since the 1970s for film preservation, including a 2018 essay for Britannica. The public page is truncated after 1978, so nothing on Raging Bull or later films was read there. Used for the achievement cards only.

The Film Foundation, press release 'Filmmakers announce new Film Foundation for film preservation' (1 May 1990) -- founding announcement by Scorsese, Woody Allen, Francis Ford Coppola, Stanley Kubrick, George Lucas, Sydney Pollack, Robert Redford and Steven Spielberg, naming Scorsese president of the board and giving the foundation's four goals (public awareness, funds for archives, joint archive-industry projects, preservation practices for current productions). Organisation's own archive page, promotional in tone; used for what was announced and when, not for how he behaved in any scene. Read in full.

Raeanne Marsh, 'Scorsese's Film Foundation Preserving Lifetime of Movies', Moving Pictures magazine (20 September 2010), republished on the Film Foundation site -- trade-magazine profile: 545 films restored since 1990, his campaign for Kodak to develop a low-fade colour stock after noticing faded prints, which he advocated during the 1980 Raging Bull press tour (the film was shot in black-and-white partly to avoid fading), how the board selects preservation projects from archives' annual proposals, and the dilemma of restoring a film as audiences first saw it or with new technology. Trade-press profile quoting him, with the foundation's own executive director; admiring in tone. Read in full.

Den of Geek, 'Thelma Schoonmaker interview: editing Silence, Scorsese, Michael Powell' (published around the release of Silence, undated on the page) -- interview with his long-time editor: dailies viewed together with him constantly telling her what he feels about what he shot, his strong views on a slower pace and a very quiet, nature-merged sound mix for Silence, his instruction to leave a noisy Taiwanese bird on the dialogue track ('That's part of it'), shooting the samurai emerging from sudden fog ('Shoot it!') and later reshooting the close-ups, his habit of showing her films as inspiration before a scene, his love of grasping accidents (the Taxi Driver mirror line), and her view that Bringing Out the Dead, King of Comedy and Raging Bull took years to be appreciated. Collaborator first-hand account (non-self), warm in tone. Read in full.

Wide Angle / Closeup, 'Interview with Editor Thelma Schoonmaker' (conducted in January 1991 on the Cape Fear set, with a second later interview) -- Schoonmaker on how they work: Scorsese and De Niro want private space because they experiment so much, he shoots knowing how the film will go together and does a lot of directing in the editing room, he likes to see all the options for each line and consults while she cuts, he rarely reshoots, he scripted Goodfellas so closely that no beloved material had to be dropped, whereas After Hours was 45 minutes too long, and his critical ear for sound ('I heard you fading'). Collaborator first-hand account (non-self), admiring but concrete. Read in full.

No Film School, ''Silence' Cinematographer Rodrigo Prieto on Shooting Film and Digital for Scorsese' (December 2016) -- cinematographer's account: Scorsese is 'very meticulous with his shot listing and diagrams', which become 'the bible' and which he made largely before the locations were fixed; if he imagines a camera move he finds it hard to shake it, though at other times he is flexible with what a location offers; he chose a simpler visual language for this story; no random camera move. The introduction notes he had tried for 27 years to get Silence made (a statement by the writer, not checked). Collaborator first-hand account (non-self), admiring. Read in full.

Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences (A.frame), 'Rodrigo Prieto on Killers of the Flower Moon' interview (2023) -- cinematographer on working with Scorsese on a fourth film: he explains the shot list to him in prep, asked 'How do we evolve that?' about the look, proposed tinting and toning as an experiment which Prieto tested and found too stylised, Petzval lenses were tested, and a film is always playing in his trailer. Institution-run interview; collaborator first-hand account (non-self), admiring. Read in full.

Rolling Stone, 'Martin Scorsese, Robert De Niro at Tribeca Film Fest: 10 Things We Learned' (April 2019) -- report of their public conversation: De Niro rehearsed the improvised Mean Streets scene with Scorsese, who jotted the details in a notebook; De Niro pushed him over several years to make Raging Bull while Scorsese hesitated; Jerry Lewis's professionalism on The King of Comedy taught him not to take an actor's time for granted. Mostly Scorsese's own recollections (self) as reported by a journalist, with De Niro present. Read in full.

Boords, 'Martin Scorsese's Hand Drawn Taxi Driver Storyboards & the Stories Behind Them' -- blog article summarising the four-minute interview with Scorsese on the Taxi Driver Collector's Edition and a Phaidon interview: he drew his own pencil storyboards (often stick figures), used them to brief the crew and cinematographer Michael Chapman, and compared them with the shot list during the shoot to decide whether to combine, push or cut shots. Secondary summary of Scorsese's own words (self), so used only in combination with the independent preparation accounts. Read in full.

WAMC (NPR) Morning Edition, 'Scorsese, Departed Grab Top Oscars' (26 February 2007) -- report that after five directing nominations he won the best director Oscar for The Departed, which also won best picture, and that he had been nominated seven times in all including twice for screenwriting; names his earlier nominated films. Read in full.

Flickr photo page 'NEG_6647 | Photo by: Neil Grabowsky | Montclair Film' (photographer credit Neil Grabowsky, Montclair Film Festival, 27 October 2023), licence shown as Creative Commons Attribution 2.0 -- page checked for the portrait's licence. Not used for any scoring.

planning_orientation.rationale: [src_scorsese_nofilmschool_prieto, src_scorsese_academy_prieto, src_scorsese_wideangle_schoonmaker, src_scorsese_boords | 1976-2023 | cinematographer + editor + his own account] Prieto says Scorsese is 'very meticulous' with shot lists and diagrams, made largely before the locations were fixed, and explains the whole shot list to him in prep; Schoonmaker says he shoots knowing how the film will go together and that on Goodfellas every shot was 'preordained' to follow the next; Scorsese says he drew his own Taxi Driver storyboards and compared them with the shot list each day. Three independent kinds of witness over more than 40 years; kept below 80 because all are admiring collaborators and some are his own words. LEAD REVIEW CORRECTION (Roster49, before eligibility, downward only): every behavioural source is an admiring collaborator with no outside critic of his method; score and confidence lowered.

detail_orientation.rationale: [src_scorsese_wideangle_schoonmaker, src_scorsese_nofilmschool_prieto, src_scorsese_dog_schoonmaker | 1991-2017 | editor + cinematographer] Schoonmaker says he has a critical ear for sound (hearing a mix 'fading') and likes to see each line's acting options in order of preference; Prieto says there is never a random camera move and that he chooses every angle; on Silence he wanted music nearly unheard and merged with natural sound. Consistent across independent collaborators, but all anecdotal and warm, hence strong inference at moderate confidence.

adaptability.rationale: [src_scorsese_dog_schoonmaker, src_scorsese_nofilmschool_prieto, src_scorsese_wideangle_schoonmaker | 1991-2017 | editor + cinematographer] On Silence, when fog suddenly whited out the village shot, he told the crew 'Shoot it!', used it, and reshot the close-ups; he told the sound man to leave a noisy bird on the dialogue track; Schoonmaker says he loves grasping accidents (the Taxi Driver mirror line); Prieto says that on the day they would adjust the shot list as they went, although at times he finds a conceived camera move hard to shake. Several separate episodes from two independent collaborators, with the rigid side of the picture noted. LEAD REVIEW CORRECTION (Roster49, before eligibility, downward only): every behavioural source is an admiring collaborator with no outside critic of his method; score and confidence lowered.

experimentation.rationale: [src_scorsese_wideangle_schoonmaker, src_scorsese_rollingstone_tribeca, src_scorsese_academy_prieto | 1973-2023 | editor + cinematographer + his own account] Schoonmaker says he and De Niro want private space because they 'experiment so much'; Scorsese says De Niro's Mean Streets improvisation was worked out in rehearsal weeks before shooting; Prieto says Scorsese brought the idea of tinting and toning for Killers of the Flower Moon ('Let's experiment with this') and had Petzval lenses tested, some of which went into the film while the tinting was dropped as too stylised. Spread over fifty years with independent and self sources. LEAD REVIEW CORRECTION (Roster49, before eligibility, downward only): every behavioural source is an admiring collaborator with no outside critic of his method; score and confidence lowered.

collaboration.rationale: [src_scorsese_wideangle_schoonmaker, src_scorsese_dog_schoonmaker, src_scorsese_academy_prieto, src_scorsese_rollingstone_tribeca | 1973-2023 | editor + cinematographer + his own account] Schoonmaker says he consults on how scenes should work, sits in the edit room while she cuts and then they look at it together; Prieto says he asked 'How do we evolve that?' about the film's look and welcomes testing his ideas; Scorsese says De Niro pushed him for years to make Raging Bull and that Jerry Lewis taught him not to take an actor's time for granted. Long repeat partnerships are consistent across sources, but every behavioural source is an admiring colleague and none an outside critic, so the score is held at 74. LEAD REVIEW CORRECTION (Roster49, before eligibility, downward only): every behavioural source is an admiring collaborator with no outside critic of his method; score and confidence lowered.

persistence.rationale: [src_scorsese_nofilmschool_prieto, src_scorsese_rollingstone_tribeca, src_scorsese_dog_schoonmaker | 1980-2016 | cinematographer + his own account + editor] The Silence introduction says he spent 27 years trying to get it made (writer's statement, not checked); Scorsese says he hesitated for years over Raging Bull and then had to persuade a studio that the project was worth it; Schoonmaker says several of their films took years to be appreciated and some were box-office disappointments. The project timelines are partly his own telling and the 27-year figure is unverified, so strong inference at modest confidence.

risk_tolerance.rationale: [src_scorsese_dog_schoonmaker, src_scorsese_britannica | 1976-2016 | editor + encyclopaedia] Schoonmaker says Bringing Out the Dead, King of Comedy and Raging Bull were disasters at the box office and that this is 'what happens when you go out on a limb'; Britannica says the risk he took with Taxi Driver was vindicated and that New York, New York, a stylised rethinking of the Hollywood musical, was a commercial flop. Outcomes mixed and partly judged by the people close to him, so dual-edged and moderate.

impact_motivation.rationale: [src_scorsese_filmfoundation_1990, src_scorsese_movingpictures, src_scorsese_britannica | 1980-2018 | foundation + trade press + encyclopaedia] The Film Foundation announced on 1 May 1990 with Scorsese as board president, to preserve American film heritage; the 2010 profile says he had campaigned for Kodak to develop a low-fade colour stock after the 1980 Raging Bull press tour and that the foundation had restored 545 films; Britannica notes his efforts since the 1970s and a 2018 essay on preservation. Documented, sustained, and directly about film heritage, but the foundation's own page and a profile built on his own account carry the detail, so confidence stays at 0.64. LEAD REVIEW CORRECTION (Roster49, before eligibility, downward only): every behavioural source is an admiring collaborator with no outside critic of his method; score and confidence lowered.

aesthetic_sensitivity.rationale: [src_scorsese_dog_schoonmaker, src_scorsese_academy_prieto, src_scorsese_nofilmschool_prieto | 2016-2023 | editor + cinematographer] Schoonmaker says he shows her films before a scene as inspiration, not to copy (an Eisenstein plate-breaking shot for Gangs of New York) and wanted Silence's music almost unheard; Prieto says he always has an old film playing in his trailer and wanted a subtle religious feeling in one shot and a simpler language for Silence. Visual and sonic form is clearly central to his decisions, but the evidence is anecdotal and from collaborators.

provenance.notes: QID VERIFIED LIVE: Wikidata wbgetentities (2026-10-11) for Q41148 returned en label 'Martin Scorsese', description 'American filmmaker (born 1942)', born 1942-11-17, no death date, citizenship United States (plus a second listed citizenship that no read source confirms, so only US is recorded), ko label present; the lead's QID hint was correct. SLUG/QID CHECK: no existing production or candidate file for this slug or QID. CANONICAL SIGNIFICANCE SOURCE: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Martin Scorsese' (https://www.britannica.com/biography/Martin-Scorsese), whose public page is truncated after 1978, supplemented for later records by the NPR/WAMC Oscars report. LIVING SUBJECT: only documented, public professional filmmaking behaviour is scored (preparation and shot-listing, set and editing-room decisions, collaboration with named colleagues, and the documented film-preservation activity). Family, marriages, religion and upbringing, health, finances, controversies over individual films, rumours and any inferred motive were excluded; Britannica's early-life, personal-life and critical-reception passages and a Rolling Stone item on a Cabinet member's comment were read and not used. READ (9 substantive behavioural or activity sources, plus Britannica, the NPR/WAMC report and Flickr for cards and rights): two Schoonmaker interviews (1991 and around 2017), two Prieto interviews (2016 and 2023), the Rolling Stone report of the Scorsese-De Niro conversation, the Boords summary of his Taxi Driver storyboard interview, the Film Foundation 1990 press release and the 2010 Moving Pictures profile. PERSPECTIVES: editor, cinematographer, a lead actor via Scorsese's account, the Film Foundation as organisation, trade and general press, an encyclopaedia and Scorsese's own recollections (self, never sole support for a row; the two Schoonmaker pieces and the two Prieto pieces are each one witness, counted once per witness). Every behavioural source is an admiring collaborator or his own foundation, with no outside critic of his working method, so no score exceeds 78 and no confidence exceeds 0.68. NOT OPENED: Paul Schrader's and De Niro's own accounts, Michael Chapman's account, the Fresh Air 2005 Schoonmaker interview (long page opened but not used), the ProVideo Coalition podcast page (only a blurb), the StudioBinder Taxi Driver article (secondary), Scorsese's own books, the documentary 'Scorsese by Ebert' and the biographies by Ian Christie, David Thompson and Mary Pat Kelly. The 27-year Silence development figure is the No Film School writer's statement and was not independently checked. PORTRAIT: Commons 'Martin Scorsese 2023.jpg' (Neil Grabowsky for Montclair Film, 27 October 2023), CC BY 2.0 per the Commons licence tag, a passed FlickreviewR check and Montclair Film's own Flickr page showing the Creative Commons Attribution 2.0 licence; no personality-rights or other restriction template is on the Commons page; downloaded at 3712 x 5568 and downscaled to 667 x 1000; the image is a studio-style press portrait against a dark background of a living sitter. LEAD REVIEW (Roster49): 5 rows lowered before eligibility because all behavioural sources are admiring collaborators.
